questions_and_answers.question_text: What are the three senses of quán?
What is Lǚxíngshè short for, and what are the two agencies?
What does gǎo mean, and what two kinds of thing can it take?
Which prepositional verb is used with mǎnyì?
Write the Chinese for "He's a translator."
Write the Chinese for "Are you satisfied with my answer?"
Write the Chinese for "This set of books is incomplete."
Which verb is gǎo interchangeable with in resultative compounds?

articles.text:
11. A: Wǒmen xiǎng qùde dìqū quán    Have you been to all the regions you
       dōu qù le ba? Hái yǒu shénme  wanted to go to? Do you have any more
       wèntí meiyou?                 questions?
    B: Méiyou shénme wèntí le,      We don't have any more questions. The
       Lǚxíngshède gōngzuò gǎode     China Travel Service did a very good
       hěn hǎo, wǒmen hěn mǎnyì.     job and we're very pleased.

Notes on No. 11

dìqū: "region," "district," "area"

Běijīng dìqū       the Běijīng area
Huáběi dìqū        the north China region
shān dìqū          a mountainous district

quán: (1) "to be complete," (2) "whole," "entire," (3) "entirely," "completely"

Zhèitào shū bù quán, dìsìběn     This set of books is incomplete; the
méiyou le.                       fourth volume is missing.
Quán shìjiè yígòng yǒu duōshao   How many languages are there in the
zhǒng yǔyán?                     whole world?

Lǚxíngshè: Short for Zhōngguó Lǚxíngshè, CHINA TRAVEL SERVICE (CTS), or Zhōngguó Guójì Lǚxíngshè, CHINA INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL SERVICE (CITS). These are the TWO GOVERNMENT AGENCIES through which ALL travel arrangements in China are handled. Representatives from CITS accompany tour groups in China.

gǎo: "to do," "to carry on," "to engage in," "to work in" a certain field.

Gǎo shénme ne?                   What are you doing? / What are you up to?

(GǍO A TASK OR ENDEAVOUR)
gǎo wèishēng          to do cleanup
gǎo shēngchǎn         to engage in production
gǎo shèhuìzhǔyì       to practice socialism
gǎo Sìge Xiàndàihuà   to carry on the Four Modernizations

(GǍO A LINE OF WORK)
Tā shi gǎo fānyìde.              He's a translator.
Tā shi gǎo wénxuéde.             He works in literature.
Tā shi gǎo xīnwénde.             He's a journalist.
Tā shi gǎo nóngyède.             He works in agriculture.

Gǎohǎo, especially common in POLITICAL talk, means "to make a good job of (something)."

Gǎo is used with many resultative verb endings (here gǎo is interchangeable with nòng):

Shéi bǎ wǒde chē gǎohuài le?     Who broke my bicycle/car?
Hài, nǐ yòu gǎocuò le.           No, you've got it wrong again.

Zěnme gǎode is an IDIOM:

Zěnme gǎode?!                    What went wrong?! / What's wrong?!
Nǐ zěnme gǎode?!                 What's with you? / What's the matter
                                 with you?

mǎnyì: "to be pleased," "to be satisfied." Often used with the prepositional verb DUÌ, equivalent to English "pleased WITH":

Wǒde huídá, nǐ mǎnyì ma?         Are you satisfied with my answer?
Tā duì nǐ zhème hǎo, nǐ          He's so good to you; why are you still
wèishénme hái bù mǎnyì?          dissatisfied?

Yíge mǎnyìde huídá is an idiom for "a satisfactory answer."
